item.title: Houthis Step Up Attacks on Saudi, Sending Oil Higher
item.description: Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen step up their attacks on Saudi Arabia. Saudi Aramco had to evacuate its headquarters and the kingdom is on alert for more strikes. The US State Department has ordered non-emergency personnel to leave the country. Oil prices are spiking. Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Retirement Longevity Risk a Top Factor for Investors
item.description: Many older Americans do not feel comfortable spending money on pleasure due to fear of outliving their savings. Costs are rising in almost every aspect of life, particularly healthcare, which eats up more of a retiree’s budget as they age. Marta Norton, Chief Investment Strategist at Empower, discusses the market landscape and how the current workforce should invest for longevity when it comes to their retirement. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Private Credit's Daily Marks Under Fire
item.description: Monroe Capital CEO Ted Koenig says daily marks on illiquid private-credit assets create an illusion of precision, not accuracy. He discusses the deal slowdown, pressure on private-equity exits and why he's cautious about data centers and GPU lending. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Spotify Rallies on Subscribers; Hermès falls on China Sales | Stock Movers
item.description: - Shares of Procter & Gamble (PG) moved higher ahead of the US market open after the company's sales and profits beat Wall Street expectations. Organic revenue rose 4% in the first quarter, the fastest growth in three years. - Shares of Spotify (SPOT) rallied after results and forecast spoke to improving margin trends. Spotify reported that the service’s paying subscribers increased 2% to hit 306 million in the third quarter, topping Wall Street estimates of 305.1 million. - Hermès (RMS FP) reported disappointing sales in the third quarter on sluggish demand in China. Their 41% slump so far this year puts them on track for the worst annual performance since the company listed in 1993. - Shares of Lam Research (LRCX) fell in premarket trading after the semiconductor capital equipment company gave a forecast for adjusted second-quarter earnings slightly weaker than expected. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ‘Paralyzed’ US IPO Market Asks If There’s Life After Anthropic
item.description: The debate over artificial intelligence is keeping IPOs stuck on the launching pad, and with the shadow of Anthropic PBC’s market debut looming larger by the day, billions of dollars of capital and months of preparations are hanging in the balance.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz

item.title: Partners’ EyeCare Set to Close Deal to Repay Debt at Discount
item.description: EyeCare Partners is set to close a deal with its creditors this week to sell assets and repay its debt at a discount, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Irene García Pérez

item.title: American Airlines Cuts Full-Year Outlook Again as Fuel Costs Climb
item.description: American Airlines cut its full-year outlook for the third time in the past six months amid persistently high fuel prices. The carrier has warned it may need to further reduce flying if prices remain elevated. Siddharth Philip reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Irmãos Moreira Salles destoam de empresários e se opõem a Flávio
item.description: Matheus Piovesana conta como os irmãos João e Walter Moreira Salles destoam de parte da elite brasileira e se opõem a Flávio Bolsonaro. Produção de Gisele Fernandes e edição de Patricia Xavier. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: South Africa Must Prioritize Growth, Finance Minister Says
item.description: South Africa has strengthened fiscal discipline and now must lift economic growth, Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana said.
item.dc:creator: Ntando Thukwana and S'thembile Cele

item.title: Copper’s AI Tailwind Faces Supply and Demand Uncertainty
item.description: At LME week, Amy Gower of Morgan Stanley said copper traders lack conviction about the metal’s direction. Copper has tracked AI stocks closely, although AI is still a small share of demand; uncertainty over possible U.S. import tariffs is also drawing large volumes of copper into the country and could redirect supply from other markets. Gower said mine supply is expected to fall this year, with further risks next year from project recoveries and potential strikes in Chile and the U.S. Other possible supports include continued tariff-related stockpiling, stronger AI demand and Chinese stimulus. But China’s end-use indicators are mixed, and weakness in construction and property remains a concern. The discussion also noted that copper’s recent gains are struggling to extend. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Banque du Caire Boosts Size of Egypt’s Biggest IPO in a Decade
item.description: Banque du Caire boosted the stake it’s offering in a long-delayed IPO to 45%, in what would be Egypt’s largest initial public offering in more than a decade.
item.dc:creator: Tarek El-Tablawy

item.title: Qatar Agrees to Buy US LNG to 2054 as War Upends Supply
item.description: QatarEnergy signed a deal with Cheniere Energy Inc. to buy 4 million tons a year of liquefied natural gas through 2054, the Middle East nation’s first such US offtake deal as its own production has been throttled by the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Liao and Stephen Stapczynski

item.title: Norwegians Leave Gold in Forest as Some Fall for Scam
item.description: Swindlers have persuaded Norwegians into buying gold and leaving it in the forest as part of a growing investment fraud, according to the country’s banking lobby.
item.dc:creator: Ott Ummelas

item.title: Stocks Drop as Risk-Off Views Dominate With Oil Up, Meta Falling
item.description: Stocks declined Thursday as escalating concern about Mideast conflict pushed oil prices higher, spurring inflation fears with US midterm elections less than two weeks away. Meta Platforms Inc. tumbled as investors parsed its results along with the rest of the latest batch of technology earnings for evidence that massive spending on AI is paying off.
item.dc:creator: Felice Maranz

item.title: Blackstone Profit Drops 9.2% as Higher Rates Curb Dealmaking
item.description: Blackstone Inc. reported a drop in third-quarter income as higher interest rates subdued dealmaking, with the money the firm deployed reaching a low for this year.
item.dc:creator: Preeti Singh

item.title: Treasuries Surge as AI Stock Jitters Fuel Haven Demand
item.description: US Treasuries rose as investors sought shelter from stock-market losses, particularly for companies with exposure to the boom in spending on artificial-intelligence assets.
item.dc:creator: David Finnerty and Ruth Carson

item.title: Gold Falls as Higher Oil Fuels Inflation Fears Ahead of Fed Meet
item.description: Gold declined to the lowest in more than two months as escalating Middle East hostilities sent oil surging ahead of a Federal Reserve policy meeting, while a selloff in equities added to broader market volatility.
item.dc:creator: Yihui Xie and Jack Ryan

item.title: Michigan, Ohio Gas Prices Jump After Illinois Refinery Upset
item.description: Gas prices in Michigan and Ohio surged following an issue at a Chicago-area refinery, further squeezing voters’ wallets in key battleground states with 12 days before US midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Will Kubzansky

item.title: Stocks Fall as AI, Oil Risks Spur Flight to Bonds: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks dropped as a jump in oil prices and renewed concerns about the outlook for the artificial-intelligence trade pushed global investors toward the safety of bonds.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 22
item.description: Oil advanced after deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia heightened concerns that escalating Middle East hostilities could hit supply, even as exports through the Strait of Hormuz accelerate.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama and Alex Longley
